verdict.rationale: Kimi's API platform lets you create multiple API keys per project and restrict each project with budgets, rate limits, an IP whitelist and membership, so a key can be isolated to a constrained project; keys can also be managed through the Admin API. However, the restrictions attach to projects rather than to permission scopes on individual keys, so true least-privilege scoping per agent credential is not documented. Missing for 10: per-key permission/endpoint scopes, agent-specific credential issuance, key expiry/TTL controls, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can create multiple projects in an organization and multiple API keys in each project
set project budgets and rate limits, manage members, configure an IP whitelist, and review organization and project consumption
The Kimi Admin API lets organization administrators manage members, invitations, projects, and inference API keys programmatically
Kimi members can create and manage API Keys in the Kimi Code Console (up to 5 keys; each is shown only once upon creation—please keep it safe).
